title: Pain on the Inside of the Elbow: Is It Golfer's Elbow, and What Helps?
metaDescription: Inner elbow pain with a weak grip may be golfer's elbow. Causes, tingling in the little finger, treatment step by step, and when to see a doctor.
intro: Pain on the inner side of the elbow with a weaker grip is usually golfer's elbow. You do not need to play golf; repeated gripping and lifting cause it. Most people recover without surgery using rest, medicines and exercises. Tingling in the ring and little fingers needs a closer look.

sections.heading: What is golfer's elbow?
sections.body: It is overuse of the forearm tendons that attach to the inner elbow. OrthoInfo says it comes on gradually over weeks to months, usually between ages 40 and 60. You may feel pain or burning, a weak grip, and sometimes stiffness.

sections.heading: How is it different from tennis elbow?
sections.body: Position. Golfer's elbow hurts on the inside of the elbow, tennis elbow on the outside. Both are overuse problems of the tendons, both usually settle without surgery, and the treatment is similar.

sections.heading: Why are my ring and little fingers tingling?
sections.body: It can mean the ulnar nerve at the elbow is irritated, which OrthoInfo notes can happen with golfer's elbow. See a doctor if the numbness is constant, the hand is getting weak or clumsy, or the fingers start to curl, so the nerve can be checked.

sections.heading: What helps?
sections.body: We usually go step by step.
bullets: Rest from the painful activity, with pain relief gels or tablets and a short spell of ice.
Then stretching and strengthening exercises, which OrthoInfo says help most, and a brace if useful.
If pain remains, physiotherapy treatments such as ultrasound or shockwave, for pain relief.
An injection only if still needed, for pain relief.

sections.heading: Do injections help?
sections.body: OrthoInfo warns that steroid injections may slow recovery and worsen tendon damage, so we use them sparingly. PRP and shockwave are options, but nobody knows yet if they beat exercises. We use them for pain relief only.

sections.heading: When is surgery needed?
sections.body: Only after several months without improvement. Most cases are treated without it. After surgery, strengthening starts at 6 to 8 weeks and normal activities return in about 3 to 6 months.

faqs.a: Repeated gripping, lifting or swinging movements that overload the inner forearm tendons.

faqs.q: How long does golfer's elbow last?
faqs.a: It varies; weeks to months, and longer if the arm is not rested.

faqs.q: Can I play golf with golfer's elbow?
faqs.a: Cut back while the pain is bad, and check your grip and technique.
Not usually, but numbness or weakness should be checked.

faqs.q: What is the difference between tennis and golfer's elbow?
